facts.about: Central Depository Services Limited is a Market Infrastructure Institution (MII), part of the capital market structure, providing services to all market participants - exchanges, clearing corporations, depository participants (DPs), issuers and investors. It is a facilitator for holding of securities in the dematerialised form and an enabler for securities transactions.

flags.text: Profit compounding (+18%/yr) lags sales (+27%/yr) over 3 years — margins under pressure
Operating margin compressed 6 pts in 3 years (57% → 51%)

business.summary: CDSL provides secure, efficient depository services, enabling dematerialisation and digitisation of securities. It supports India's securities markets through technology-driven infrastructure, including e-CAS, e-DIS, and online account opening, ensuring safe custody and seamless transfer of assets for investors.

segments.name: Depository Activity
segments.note: Core business providing depository services for securities.

segments.name: Data Entry and Storage
segments.note: Centralized record keeping of KYC documents for investors.

segments.name: Repository
segments.note: Electronic storage for insurance policies and warehouse receipts.

scorecard.promised: Long-term sustainable growth creating value proposition for the market.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue grew 23.5% YoY to ₹394 cr in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue increased from ₹319 cr in Sep 2025 to ₹394 cr in Sep 2026, a 23.5% YoY jump.

scorecard.promised: Infrastructure costs are not always commensurate with revenue growth due to capacity building.
scorecard.delivered: Annual operating margin compressed from 58% in FY25 to 51% in FY26.
scorecard.evidence: Operating margin dropped 7 percentage points annually as profit compounding (+18%) lagged sales growth (+27%) over 3 years.

scorecard.promised: Maintaining 80% plus market share with incremental share of 85% to 90%.
scorecard.delivered: Management claims dominant market share of over 80% in demat accounts.
scorecard.evidence: Claimed 80%+ total and 85-90% incremental share despite analyst pushback on incremental losses in Q1 FY27.

scorecard.promised: Continuous investment in technology for system resilience and scalability.
scorecard.delivered: Capital work in progress stands at ₹12 cr as of Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Management prioritizes infrastructure over quarterly expense fluctuations; FCF remains healthy at ₹346 cr in FY26.

scorecard.promised: KRA rack rates reduced to INR5 for creation and INR28 for fetching.
scorecard.delivered: Regulatory pricing reset implemented across the industry.
scorecard.evidence: Management confirmed the lower rates in Q2 FY27 following the industry-wide regulatory change.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully scaled revenue and maintained market dominance, though aggressive technology spending has led to visible margin compression.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Technology spend is an investment in future scale and not always commensurate with revenue.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Annual net profit fell from ₹526 cr (FY25) to ₹455 cr (FY26) despite revenue rising.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Employee cost increases are driven by annual appraisal cycles in Q1.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Margins dipped to 47% in Jun 2026 (Q1) from 58% in Sep 2024.

bull: Revenue reached a record ₹394 cr in Sep 2026, representing 23.5% YoY growth.
Strong cash generation with a 5-year cash conversion rate at 97% of PAT.
Debt-free balance sheet with net worth growing to ₹1,984 cr by Sep 2026.
bear: Operating margins have compressed significantly, falling from 66% in FY22 to 51% in FY26.
Net profit for FY26 (₹455 cr) declined 13.5% from FY25 levels (₹526 cr).
KRA revenue faces headwinds from regulatory price caps on creation and fetching charges.
watch: Recovery of operating margins toward the 60% historical average in upcoming quarters.
Impact of regulatory supervision on ISIN issuance for unlisted companies.
Sustainability of the 80% market share amid rising competitive intensity.

claims.claim: Management continues to invest in technology to ensure system resilience and efficiency as market activity evolves.
claims.quote: We continue to embark on this journey to ensure that the robustness and the resiliency of the CDSL system remains top notch and continues to work on that.

claims.claim: The rack rates for KRA services are INR5 for creation and INR28 for fetching.
claims.quote: For creation, it has come down to INR5. And for fetching it has come down to INR28.

claims.claim: Higher KRA expenses are driven by increased interoperability costs and Aadhaar-based eKYC charges payable to UIDAI.
claims.quote: On the KRA side, the other expenses have increased primarily because the interoperability expenses have increased with the increase in fetch volumes.

claims.claim: The ability to issue ISINs for unlisted companies is currently under regulatory supervision.
claims.quote: It is going through the regulatory supervision, and it's in that process.

claims.claim: The company prioritizes maintaining infrastructure and value proposition over managing quarter-on-quarter technology expense fluctuations.
claims.quote: Rather than seeing it as a quarter-on-quarter, you have to see in terms of the stakeholder interest growing, number of accounts growing and that value proposition should remain intact.

claims.claim: Management views growth as a long-term sustainable process rather than focusing on quarter-on-quarter market share fluctuations.
claims.quote: Our intent at least CDSL is not a quarter-on-quarter growth. It is a long-term sustainable growth, which creates value proposition for the market.

claims.claim: Quarterly employee cost increases are primarily driven by the annual appraisal cycle and variable pay payouts.
claims.quote: So, the appraisal has got done in this quarter, which has just ended, and all the variable pay, et cetera, is paid in this quarter.

claims.claim: Technology is the core DNA of the business, requiring continuous investment to maintain scalability and value proposition.
claims.quote: I think one needs to see this business, and I have been talking about this, that technology is the DNA of our business. It's kind of the Raw Material, Work in Progress, and Finished goods.

claims.claim: CDSL maintains a dominant market share of over 80% in demat accounts.
claims.quote: maintaining our 80% plus market share with a consistently incremental market share of 85% to 90%, supported by the continuous trust of investors and depository participants on our platform.

claims.claim: The reduction in KYC fetch and creation charges is an industry-wide regulatory change.
claims.quote: It's going to be across basically the industry. So, it is not only for CVL.

claims.claim: Pricing changes require SEBI approval and are focused on balancing inclusivity with service quality.
claims.quote: So there needs a prior approval or any change upward or downward, obviously, after deliberation by the honourable CDSL Board, but it has to be then proposed to SEBI for it to be approved.

claims.claim: Infrastructure investment is necessary to maintain a seamless experience and keep pace with innovation, AI, and regulatory requirements.
claims.quote: The process of ensuring that a seamless experience is there for all the participants is our intent and all basically will be able to see their holdings, etc., in a very seamless manner is what is basically the intent.

claims.claim: Additions of unlisted companies are circumstance-driven, occurring primarily when companies need to raise or transfer capital.
claims.quote: But again, those conditions remain only when they want to raise capital, or they want to transfer capital. So those are very circumstance driven as to when they are mandated to be registered with us.

claims.claim: The company must maintain robust infrastructure regardless of market cycles to be prepared for sudden growth spurts.
claims.quote: As a market infrastructure provider, we are continuing to build on our systems, whether we have a great period or a lean period because when the growth comes, it comes all of a sudden.

claims.claim: Infrastructure costs are not always commensurate with revenue growth because they involve building capacity for future scale.
claims.quote: And the investment is in a larger proportion to the growth which you see. It's not commensurate with the growth you're seeing because it's kind of building a road.

risks.text: Contingent liabilities include bank guarantees totaling 710.46 lakh as of March 31, 2026.
Related party transactions include purchases (0.29%) and sales (0.46%) of total values.
Auditor identified IT systems and controls as a key audit matter due to transaction volume.
